info.title: FileSquid API
info.description: The single FileSquid API served by every FileSquid host. See resources/architecture/030-filesquid-api-and-transports.md. Conventions: a command (mutation) sends a CommandEnvelope as the `envelope` member of its JSON request body (operation_id is the idempotency key, expected_revision the revision last read) and answers with a CommandOutcome; a query (list) takes the PageSize (`limit`, 1-1000) and Cursor (`cursor`) parameters; every failed request answers with an ApiError body (code, message, retryable). Router-wide fallbacks: any /api/v1/ path not in this contract answers 404 not_found, and a documented path called with a method it does not document answers 405 method_not_allowed; both carry the ApiError body. They are not listed per operation because no operation sends them. Authorisation is deny-by-default: every operation, including health, the contract and the event channel, requires the bearerAuth credential and is authorised before anything else runs, so a call without it answers 401 unauthorized and a call whose credential is not accepted or does not grant the operation answers 403 forbidden, before any 404 or 405; both carry the ApiError body with a DenialReason in `reason`. Each operation names the authorisation action it performs in x-filesquid-action. The one deliberate exception is GET /api/v1/health/live (x-filesquid-action public, security []), a liveness probe that answers only {"status":"up"} without a credential. The content route GET and HEAD /api/v1/content/{handle} (x-filesquid-action content.read, x-filesquid-credential content-handle, security []) is not public: its only credential is the content handle in its path, minted by POST /api/v1/content-handles for one file version (API-S-018); a Bearer token is not accepted there, and every unusable request under /api/v1/content/ (unknown, malformed, missing, expired, evicted or revoked handle, an extra path segment or another method) answers one identical 403 forbidden with reason invalid_credentials, never 401, 404 or 405. Paths marked x-filesquid-host-route are served by the hosts, not by the filesquid-api router.

get.summary: Process health
Liveness probe: the process is up (public, no credential)
get.description: Deliberately public so process supervisors and load balancers can probe without a token. Answers only that the process is up: no version, no component detail, no journal. Full health is GET /api/v1/health, which needs the bearerAuth credential.

get.summary: This API contract
Host descriptor: host type, operator name and hosted backup and sync state
get.description: Which host this API runs on (host_type, supplied by the host when it starts, never derived from the request), who operates it (operator_name, a server's FILESQUID_OPERATOR_NAME; null on desktop and browser hosts and on an unnamed server) and the state of encrypted backup and sync to the ciphertext-only hosted service (hosted_service; backup and sync are reported separately because they are distinct guarantees). Every caller the host authenticates may read it (action host.read is granted to every accepted credential, not to administrators only); it is never public. A host.change event carries the whole new descriptor whenever a field changes; a client MUST read this route again after events.resync or a reconnect. A successful read is not journaled. The descriptor carries no token, content handle, key or key identifier, account or device identifier, e-mail address, quota, object count, size, timestamp, path or file name.

get.summary: Push events (WebSocket on filesquid-server; Tauri events named filesquid-event on filesquid-desktop).

101.description: Switching protocols to WebSocket. Each text frame is one ApiEvent.

get.description: One event channel for job progress and change notifications. Each event is an ApiEvent whose topic is an EventTopic; x-filesquid-event-payloads names the payload schema of each topic. Events are hints, not state: a client MUST NOT depend on receiving every event. A subscriber that falls more than 256 events behind, or whose next event encodes to more than 65536 bytes, receives one events.resync event (EventResync) instead of the events it missed and MUST reread the state it shows through the request routes; a client that reconnects MUST do the same. At most 64 subscribers are served at once. Authorisation: send Authorization: Bearer <token>; a browser, which cannot set headers on a WebSocket, offers the subprotocols filesquid.events.v1 and filesquid.bearer.<token> instead, and the server selects filesquid.events.v1. A refused upgrade answers 401 or 403 with an ApiError body instead of switching protocols.

get.summary: List one folder of an object version, by path or by navigation node
get.description: The folders and files directly below a logical-path prefix, folders first, with an opaque cursor; limit 1-1000, default 200. The folder is named either by library_id and object_id with an optional prefix, or by one collection or folder navigation node (API-S-021), never both (400 invalid_request otherwise). A collection or folder node is listed from the host's index of registered files where it keeps one (Task DE-1.7, ADR 041): the node's subfolders, implied by the collection logical paths of ordinary files (a folder implied only by hidden or deleted files is left out), by name in code-point order, then its registered ordinary files by name, each from its own object (`object_id`) and shown under its name in the collection; such a node takes no version, and a cursor of another listing is refused 400 invalid_request. A node must be readable to the caller: an unknown, malformed or unreadable node, or one no object holds, answers one identical 404 not_found; a library, virtual collection or repository node answers 400 invalid_request. The reserved folders provenance (PROV-O records) and .filesquid (application data) are left out of the root's page, so a page may hold fewer entries than asked while next_cursor remains; a prefix inside them answers 404. Answers storage facts only; a successful read is not journaled, a refusal is journaled once (API-S-017).

get.summary: Download one whole file version, streamed

Through the desktop scheme every answer is capped at 16 MiB (DE-S-005), so the desktop UI saves larger files with ranged reads of GET /api/v1/files/content. A successful read is not journaled, a refusal is journaled once (API-S-017). A download that starts is journaled as `file.download` (journal-only, no PROV-O record) with the caller, library, object and version (API-S-028).

put.summary: Upload one file as its own object, or new content for an existing file
put.description: The body is `multipart/form-data` with exactly three parts: `envelope` (JSON), `input` (JSON, the upload's facts) and `file` (the bytes, at most 64 MiB). Without `file_id`, the upload creates the file's own OCFL object `files/<file-id>` (identifier `urn:uuid:<file-id>`, a new UUID v4) with the original at `original/<file-uuid>.<ext>` and its metadata record (the `filesquid-metadata` file record, API-S-026) beside it in v1, never at a logical path the client chooses. With `file_id`, it is a new version of that file's object: the new bytes at the same stored path and one more import entry; the display name and statements stay. The record holds the facts the client provides (name and its normalisation form, size, last-modified time, media type) and lists every other fact as unavailable (MD-S-013). The verified size is the size of the `file` part: a declared `size` that differs fails verification, is refused (400) and commits nothing. Publishes exactly one OCFL version through the filesquid-ocfl change model, or is refused without publishing (API-S-008). The upload is journaled as `file.upload` with opaque IDs only; a refusal is journaled once. Command (Task API-F2.13, API-S-002): the body carries a `CommandEnvelope` beside the input (schema version 1; an opaque operation_id of 1 to 128 letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` or `:`; scope `library:<library_id>`). The expected revision is the head version of the file's object for an upload with `file_id`, and `0` for a new file. A stale revision is answered 409 with a `conflict` outcome and changes nothing. A 200 answer is a `CommandOutcome` of the same operation_id (`committed`) whose `result` is what the command made. A repeated operation_id of the same command that changed something answers its first answer again, before the revision is checked, with no second change; the same operation_id with another route, library or input is refused (400). A refusal stores no receipt, so its retry is evaluated again. Receipts are kept in memory while the host runs, at most 10,000. Destination and home (an upload with `file_id` keeps its home) (Task API-F2.14, API-S-011, API-S-026): the input names `collection_id` (required) and optionally `folder`; without a collection the request is refused 400 invalid_request (`destination_required`) and an unknown or foreign collection 404 not_found (`collection_not_found`), each before any byte is staged and journaled once. After the file's object is committed, the file is registered in the collection snapshot with its home collection, its logical path `<folder>/<name>` and its object, under the request's operation ID, as one snapshot version journaled `library.files.register`; the answer's `collection_id` and `path` name where it went. A path already taken in the collection, a recoverably deleted file's included, is never refused or overwritten: the new file takes the first free number beside it (`photo-1.jpg`, `archive-1.tar.gz`, `report-1`, `.env-1`, `.config-1.json`); after 9,999 numbers the request is refused 409 conflict (`path_suffix_exhausted`) and a numbered name over 255 bytes 400 invalid_request (`name_too_long`), with no change. A crash between the file's object and its registration leaves the operation's reserved file ID; a retry under the same operation ID completes that file once. Each success publishes `navigation.change` for the folder that holds the file. A host without home collections answers 503.

200.description: The version published in the file's object.

post.summary: Create a folder (pending until a file is added)
post.description: Writes nothing: OCFL stores no empty folder, so a new folder stays pending in the client and is persisted only when a file is added beneath its prefix. A file at the path or at a parent of it is a conflict. Command (Task API-F2.13, API-S-002): the body carries a `CommandEnvelope` beside the input (schema version 1; an opaque operation_id of 1 to 128 letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` or `:`; scope `library:<library_id>`). The expected revision is the head version of `object_id` that the caller read (`v1`, `v2`, ...). A stale revision is answered 409 with a `conflict` outcome and changes nothing. A 200 answer is a `CommandOutcome` of the same operation_id (`committed`) whose `result` is what the command made. A repeated operation_id of the same command that changed something answers its first answer again, before the revision is checked, with no second change; the same operation_id with another route, library or input is refused (400). Creating a folder writes nothing, so it never stores a receipt: a repeated operation_id is evaluated again.

200.description: Whether the folder exists or stays pending.

A file object's stored original (`original/` of `files/<file-id>`) never moves: such a move is refused (400) with a pointer to `POST /api/v1/files/renames`, since a rename changes only the display name (API-S-027). post.summary: Mint a content handle for one file version
post.description: For media elements (img, video, audio, source), which cannot send Authorization (API-S-018, ADR 030 Decision 5). Authorised exactly like the ranged read of that file version (action files.read; a refusal is the refusal that read gets); a content handle cannot mint another. The handle is 256 bits from the operating system's CSPRNG; the API keeps only its SHA-256 digest, in memory. At most 1,024 live handles per credential: another mint evicts the least recently used one. Journaled as api.content_handle.issued (actor, library, object, version and expiry; never the handle).

200.description: The handle, its URL and its absolute expiry.

get.summary: Read one file version through a content handle
get.description: Serves only the file version the handle names, with the ranged read's single-range handling and 16 MiB cap. The handle is accepted at the start of each request: 300 s after its mint or last accepted request, or 3,600 s after its mint, or once its minting credential ends or may no longer read files, it is refused; an answer that has started is never cut off. Every answer, denials included, carries Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, Cache-Control: private, no-store, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox.

get.summary: Open OCFL validation findings and validation runs
get.description: API-S-022. The open findings of every open library (at most 1,000, ordered by library, object, code and location; `truncated` when more are open) the schedule and cap in force and, per open library, whether a run is going, the last run and the next scheduled run. A finding's `location` is null for a caller who may not read the object: the server administrator, until per-object permissions arrive.

post.summary: Start OCFL validation runs
post.description: API-S-022. Starts a validation run of the named library, or of every open library when the body is empty or names none. A run continues from the library's stored cursor unless `from_start` is true. Runs go in the background and report in the process registry (`ocfl.validation`) and on the event channel. Starting a job changes no library content or organisation, so the body is a RunRequest, not a CommandEnvelope. Every refusal is journaled as `ocfl.validation.run`.

200.description: The libraries whose run started, and those refused.

404.description: The named library is not open on this host (`not_found`).

409.description: A run of the named library is already going (`already_running`).

put.summary: Change the OCFL validation schedule and cap
put.description: API-S-022. The desktop owner or a server administrator changes the time between scheduled runs and the object cap of a run. The next scheduled run of each open library moves with the new interval. Answers the settings now in force. Changing settings changes no library content or organisation, so the body is the settings, not a CommandEnvelope. Every change and refusal is journaled as `ocfl.validation.configure`.

get.summary: List one level of the navigation tree
get.description: One level of the tree a UI shows as its navigation and breadcrumb (API-S-021). Without node: the host's one repository. With node: that node's children - a repository's libraries; a library's collections, then its virtual collections, then the folders its unfiled files imply; a collection's folders; a folder's subfolders; nothing under a virtual collection; never files. A folder exists only when committed ordinary files imply it, so one implied only by hidden or deleted files is not listed. Every node carries an opaque handle (at most 512 bytes, never a path, storage key, SQL or token), its kind, its name and has_children (true only when the caller may read a child). ancestors holds the nodes from the repository down to and including the listed node, for the breadcrumb. Paging: limit 1-1000 (default 200) and an opaque cursor, in a stable order - the fixed kind order library, collection, virtual_collection, folder; libraries, collections and virtual collections in catalog order; folders by name in Unicode code-point order; no repeat or gap across pages. A page may hold fewer nodes than limit while next_cursor is present (nodes the caller may not read are skipped); keep following next_cursor until it is null. Only nodes the caller may read are listed, counted or named in an ancestor trail; an unknown node and one the caller may not read, or one under an unreadable ancestor, get the same 404 not_found. A folder whose handle would exceed 512 bytes cannot be named and is not listed. A malformed cursor, a cursor of another level, a limit outside 1-1000 or an unknown parameter answers 400 invalid_request. A successful read is not journaled; a refusal is journaled once as navigation.list (API-S-017). Subscribe to navigation.change on the event channel to know when to read a level again.

200.description: One page of one level of the tree.

post.summary: Create a library in an empty folder
post.description: Makes the folder the host registered as location_id the OCFL 1.1 storage root of a library: writes only the 0=ocfl_1.1 declaration, never over an existing file, and needs no account or connection (F-001). Answers the library ID (library_id when given, else a new UUID v4), which stays bound to the location until the host stops. Takes a CommandEnvelope beside its input (Task API-F2.19, API-S-002): scope location:<location_id>, expected_revision 0 (the library does not exist yet; any other value is a conflict). Answers a committed CommandOutcome for the envelope's operation_id with the library as result, at revision 1; a repeated operation_id answers the first answer again with no second change (the receipt is answered before the revision is checked), and a stale revision or any other 409 refusal is a conflict outcome beside the ApiError fields. Refusals: invalid_location, invalid_library, location_not_found, location_in_use, library_already_open, too_many_libraries (at most 64 open libraries) and root_not_empty. The outcome is journaled as library.root.create. Every refusal is journaled once, with its error code and opaque IDs only (an authorisation refusal as api.auth.denied); answers carry opaque library and object identifiers, never a filesystem path, storage key or OCFL content path (API-S-005, API-S-025).

200.description: The library created, as a committed outcome.

post.summary: Open the library in a folder
post.description: Opens the OCFL storage root in the folder the host registered as location_id through the engine's guards, and binds the library ID to it: the library its collection snapshot names (a moved or copied folder keeps its library), else library_id when given, else a new UUID v4. A library_id other than the snapshot's is refused (library_mismatch); a second folder of a library that is already open is refused (library_already_open), so two folders never share one index (ADR 041 Decision 6). Writes and repairs nothing. Opening a location that is already open answers its library again. Takes a CommandEnvelope beside its input (Task API-F2.19, API-S-002): scope location:<location_id>, expected_revision 0 for a library not open on this host, or the current revision of a library already open at that location, which is answered again (a name it gives that replaces the known one renames the library and advances its revision; otherwise nothing changes and no receipt is stored); any other value is a conflict. Answers a committed CommandOutcome for the envelope's operation_id with the library as result; a repeated operation_id of a fresh open answers the first answer again. Refusals: invalid_location, invalid_library, location_not_found, location_in_use, library_already_open, library_mismatch, too_many_libraries, not_a_storage_root and git_in_root. Only a failure is journaled, as library.root.open. Every refusal is journaled once, with its error code and opaque IDs only (an authorisation refusal as api.auth.denied); answers carry opaque library and object identifiers, never a filesystem path, storage key or OCFL content path (API-S-005, API-S-025).

200.description: The library opened, as a committed outcome.

post.summary: Plan an import of files or a folder the owner picks in the host's dialog
post.description: API-S-036. The host shows its own native dialog for the source named (`files` or `folder`) and, before any byte is staged, plans the import of what the owner picked into the open library (owner answer 5 of 2026-10-22, "Keep the review"): the answer is `pending` with `import: planned`, the `plan_id` and the `plan` the UI shows (files found, new and already in this library, bytes to copy, the destination, the count of names to be numbered, free bytes after the upload and the staging limit). `GET /api/v1/imports/{plan_id}/items` pages the planned files; the job starts only on `POST /api/v1/imports/{plan_id}/start`; `DELETE /api/v1/imports/{plan_id}` discards the plan, as the host does on its own after 1 hour. A host without the review (the desktop until Task DE-1.8) starts the job at once and answers `import: started` with the job. The body carries a CommandEnvelope whose scope is `library:<library_id>`; its operation ID is the idempotency key, so a repeated operation ID answers its open plan (`planned`, the same `plan_id`), its started job (`started`) or `cancelled` without a second dialog, and 404 not_found (`plan_not_found`) once its plan expired or was discarded. An import only adds new files, so the expected revision is not compared. `committed` with `import: cancelled` when the owner closed the dialog: no plan and no job were made. No path, file name or storage key crosses the API in the request, the answer, an error or the journal. Every import names its destination (owner decision 2026-10-22, "Must choose", ADR 041): `collection_id` and optionally `folder`. A request without `collection_id` is refused 400 invalid_request (`destination_required`) and an unknown collection 404 not_found (`collection_not_found`), each before any dialog and journaled once. Each imported file is registered in its home collection at its logical path in the library's collection snapshot under the request's operation ID. A request while a dialog is open is refused 409 conflict (`dialog_open`); a library that is not open answers 404 not_found; a host without an import dialog (filesquid-server) answers 503 unavailable. Each plan request is journaled once as `import.plan` (`succeeded` with the plan ID, `cancelled`, or `failed` with its code; `import.start` with the job ID when the host started at once); each file as `import.file`.

200.description: The plan awaiting the owner's confirmation, the job of a host without the review, or that the owner cancelled.

404.description: The library is not open on this host (`library_not_found`), the destination collection is unknown, of another library or not readable (`collection_not_found`), or the repeated operation ID's plan expired or was discarded (`plan_not_found`).

409.description: A dialog is already open (`conflict`, journal code `dialog_open`), or the operation ID already started an import of another library, destination or kind of source (`conflict`, journal code `operation_reused`).

post.summary: Copy a completed snapshot to an empty folder
post.description: Copies the committed files of every object of the open library into the empty folder the host registered as destination_location_id, never over an existing file, and validates the copy, so it is a checked OCFL root ordinary tools can read (F-042). The library is only read. Takes a CommandEnvelope beside its input (Task API-F2.19, API-S-002): scope library:<library_id>, expected_revision the library's current revision (LibraryView.revision); a stale one is a conflict outcome with no change. Answers a committed CommandOutcome for the envelope's operation_id with the report as result; the copy stores a receipt, so a repeated operation_id answers it again with no second write. Refusals: library_not_open, location_not_found, destination_overlaps_library (the destination is the folder of an open library, or inside or around one), destination_not_empty, snapshot_unreadable and snapshot_incomplete (retryable while a head is being published). The outcome is journaled as library.snapshot.copy. Every refusal is journaled once, with its error code and opaque IDs only (an authorisation refusal as api.auth.denied); answers carry opaque library and object identifiers, never a filesystem path, storage key or OCFL content path (API-S-005, API-S-025).

200.description: What the copy wrote and what its validation found, as a committed outcome.

post.summary: Rebuild a library from its files as a durable job
post.description: Starts the rebuild from files as a durable job of kind library.rebuild (API-S-025 Rebuild as a job, API-S-033) and answers pending with its job ID: the job reads every object of the open library from its OCFL files alone, so a host can rebuild its catalog without its database, reports its progress in objects (done of total) on the job routes and the job.update event, and is paused, resumed from its checkpoint without reading a completed object again, and cancelled through the job routes (API-S-037). Once the job has completed, its view's result is the RebuildReport: the objects read, the objects not readable, and each object's validation errors; an object whose head has no version inventory is flagged. Validation errors are reported, never adopted or repaired, and nothing is written to the library's files, so a cancel changes none of them. A library whose rebuild job is unfinished answers that job again, and no second job is submitted. scheduled says whether the job was handed to the host's runner now; false leaves it pending (paused, already running, or a host without a runner for the kind). The request takes a CommandEnvelope beside its input (Task API-F2.19, API-S-002): scope library:<library_id>, expected_revision the library's current revision (LibraryView.revision); a stale one is a conflict outcome and submits no job. The answer is a pending CommandOutcome for the envelope's operation_id with the job as result: a new job carries that operation_id and stores a receipt, so a repeated operation_id answers the same job; an unfinished job is answered under the request's operation_id and stores none. Refusals before any job is submitted: library_not_open, a malformed body (invalid_request), and a host without a job service (unavailable). The finished rebuild is journaled once as library.rebuild, and its job's state changes as job.*; every refusal is journaled once, with its error code and opaque IDs only (an authorisation refusal as api.auth.denied); answers carry opaque library, job and object identifiers, never a filesystem path, storage key or OCFL content path (API-S-005, API-S-025).

200.description: The rebuild's job, as a pending outcome.

get.summary: Objects whose head has no version inventory
get.description: The objects of the open library whose committed head lacks its version inventory or its sidecar (W010): what the UI may offer to repair, at most 1,000 (OCFL-S-020, API-S-023). Writes and repairs nothing. Refusals: library_not_open and the open errors of the storage root. Only a failure is journaled, as library.repair_candidates. Every refusal is journaled once, with its error code and opaque IDs only (an authorisation refusal as api.auth.denied); answers carry opaque library and object identifiers, never a filesystem path, storage key or OCFL content path (API-S-005, API-S-025).

post.summary: Repair the version inventory of named objects, with the owner's consent
post.description: The one command that adds a file to an existing version directory: for each named object whose committed head has no version inventory, adds one copy of the root inventory and its sidecar to the head version directory, then commits a new version recording the repair to the object's history (API-S-028); no file content changes (OCFL-S-020, API-S-023). Only a library's owner may run it: the desktop owner; on filesquid-server every caller, the administrator included, is refused 403 not_permitted until server accounts give a library owner a principal. The request names the library and 1 to 1,000 distinct objects and carries the owner's consent to statement version_inventory_repair.v2 (a consent to v1, which did not name the history version, is refused consent_mismatch) for exactly those objects; without it the request is refused (consent_required, consent_mismatch) and nothing is written. Each object gets its own outcome in the answer: an object whose head already holds its version inventory and sidecar is refused nothing_to_repair, never repaired. The consent and each object's outcome are journaled as ocfl.repair.version_inventory (opaque IDs, version, outcome, error code). Refusals of the whole request: invalid_objects, consent_required, consent_mismatch, library_not_open and the open errors of the storage root. Every refusal is journaled once, with its error code and opaque IDs only (an authorisation refusal as api.auth.denied); answers carry opaque library and object identifiers, never a filesystem path, storage key or OCFL content path (API-S-005, API-S-025).

200.description: One outcome per requested object, in request order.

put.summary: Set or clear the label of one version after commit
put.description: Commits one version (operation kind label) holding the object's application-data file .filesquid/labels.json, which maps labelled versions to their later labels; null clears a commit-time label. That version's own message carries no label. The file is recovered with the object from an ordinary copy. At most 1,000 labelled versions per object. A label that would not change what the version shows is refused (409) without publishing. Labels never affect retention. With provenance configured the version carries its PROV-O record (API-S-028). Journaled with opaque IDs only; a refusal is journaled once. Command (Task API-F2.13, API-S-002): the body carries a `CommandEnvelope` beside the input (schema version 1; an opaque operation_id of 1 to 128 letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` or `:`; scope `library:<library_id>`). The expected revision is the head version of `object_id` that the caller read (`v1`, `v2`, ...). A stale revision is answered 409 with a `conflict` outcome and changes nothing. A 200 answer is a `CommandOutcome` of the same operation_id (`committed`) whose `result` is what the command made. A repeated operation_id of the same command that changed something answers its first answer again, before the revision is checked, with no second change; the same operation_id with another route, library or input is refused (400). A refusal stores no receipt, so its retry is evaluated again. Receipts are kept in memory while the host runs, at most 10,000.

get.summary: The bytes one file's history keeps
get.description: The versions that changed the file, its distinct contents and their bytes, each content counted once (SRS-F-065). A successful read is not journaled; a refusal is journaled once.

get.summary: The bytes a library's history keeps
get.description: Every object's distinct contents and their bytes, each content of an object counted once, within 10,000 objects and 100,000 contents (truncated says when a bound stopped the count). Nothing is deleted, expired or thinned to free space. A successful read is not journaled; a refusal is journaled once.

post.summary: Journal the UI's console warnings and errors
post.description: API-S-030. At most 20 events and 16 KiB per request; each event becomes its own journal entry (ui.console.warn, ui.console.error or ui.console.overflow), journaled once per client event ID, and the batch is acknowledged only after the entries are stored. 60 requests a minute per credential, refused requests included; a request that carries only one overflow event naming no other principal is exempt. An event naming another principal than the credential's is refused (403, journaled).

200.description: Every event of the batch is journaled.

get.summary: Read the caller's UI preferences
get.description: The caller's own saved preferences (API-S-011, SRS-F-062), or the defaults when they saved none. A successful read is not journaled, a refusal is journaled once (API-S-017).

put.description: Replace the caller's own preferences with a complete, checked value: every field, schema 1, navigation version 1, at most 100 pinned node handles, 16 section ids of 1 to 64 characters and 1,000 collapsed node handles, each once (UI-S-017). Node entries must be handles the navigation listing wrote; no name, title, logical path, token or content handle is stored. Each pin's kind must be the kind its handle names. A host that keeps preferences for no more users answers 409 conflict (not retryable). A save is journaled once as preferences.update with the actor only, never the values.

get.summary: Read a file's statements
get.description: The populated `exif:`, `dcterms:`, `schema:` and registered extension statements of a file's metadata record, at a version or its head, each marked extracted or asserted. A successful read is not journaled; a refusal is journaled once (API-S-017).

put.summary: Set one statement of a file
put.description: Set or replace one statement in the file's metadata record. Unknown `dcterms:` names and unregistered prefixes are refused (400), naming the prefix. Publishes exactly one OCFL version through the metadata module's `ocfl` store with the caller as the version user, or is refused without publishing (409 when nothing would change or another writer moved the record first). The version is journaled with opaque IDs only; a refusal is journaled once.

post.summary: Remove one statement of a file
post.description: Remove one statement from the file's metadata record; a statement the record does not hold is 404. Publishes exactly one OCFL version through the metadata module's `ocfl` store with the caller as the version user, or is refused without publishing (409 when nothing would change or another writer moved the record first). The version is journaled with opaque IDs only; a refusal is journaled once.

get.summary: Find where a term name can go
get.description: The add order of a bare term name: `dcterms:` when the `/terms/` register knows it, then the Schema.org suggestion, then each registered extension or custom namespace that accepts it. A successful read is not journaled; a refusal is journaled once (API-S-017).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The bare term name, 1 to 128 bytes without `:`.

get.summary: List a library's registered namespaces
get.description: The library's namespace registry; empty when none was registered. A successful read is not journaled; a refusal is journaled once (API-S-017).

post.summary: Register a namespace
post.description: Register an extension namespace (IRI and optional term list) or a custom namespace as the owner, in the library's `namespaces.md` (MD-S-012). A prefix already registered is 409. Publishes exactly one OCFL version through the metadata module's `ocfl` store with the caller as the version user, or is refused without publishing (409 when nothing would change or another writer moved the record first). The version is journaled with opaque IDs only; a refusal is journaled once.

200.description: The version published in the collection snapshot.

get.summary: Read the facts of a file's import record
get.description: The read-only projection of the file's metadata record: original name, display name, extension, format and media type, size and SHA-256, and per acquisition the import time, method, storage, the path relative to the import root, the volume name and the OCFL object and version. It never answers an absolute path, import root, host or account name, and no route edits it (API-S-027, MD-S-013). A successful read is not journaled; a refusal is journaled once (API-S-017).

post.summary: Rename a file
post.description: Set the display name of a file object's original (API-S-027): the record's display name changes and nothing else, so the stored name, the logical path, the original name and every import entry stay. Publishes exactly one new version of the file's metadata record through the metadata module's `ocfl` store with the caller as the version user, or is refused without publishing (400 for an empty name, one over 1,024 bytes or one with `/` or NUL; 409 when the name is already the display name or another writer moved the record first). The version is journaled as `files.rename` with opaque IDs only; a refusal is journaled once. Command (Task API-F2.13, API-S-002): the body carries a `CommandEnvelope` beside the input (schema version 1; an opaque operation_id of 1 to 128 letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` or `:`; scope `library:<library_id>`). The expected revision is the head version of the file's object `urn:uuid:<file_id>` that the caller read. A stale revision is answered 409 with a `conflict` outcome and changes nothing. A 200 answer is a `CommandOutcome` of the same operation_id (`committed`) whose `result` is what the command made. A repeated operation_id of the same command that changed something answers its first answer again, before the revision is checked, with no second change; the same operation_id with another route, library or input is refused (400). A refusal stores no receipt, so its retry is evaluated again. Receipts are kept in memory while the host runs, at most 10,000.

post.summary: Start the PROV-O history backfill
post.description: API-S-029. The desktop owner or a server administrator starts one backfill over every OCFL storage root the host serves, in the background, and the route answers 200 at once. Each run registers in the process registry (`prov.backfill`), checkpoints per object, stops at its cap or on cancel (the host's exit), skips versions that already have a record, and commits one provenance-only version per object. The request carries no body. A request while a backfill runs is refused 409 conflict. The request is journaled once as `history.backfill.request` (succeeded, or failed with its error code: `backfill_running`, `unavailable`); each run journals itself. Starting a job changes no library content or organisation, so there is no CommandEnvelope.

200.description: The backfill started in the background.

409.description: A history backfill is already running (`conflict`).

post.summary: Let the owner pick a folder in the host's dialog
post.description: API-S-025. The host shows its own native folder dialog for the purpose named (an empty folder for a new library, a folder that holds a library, or an empty folder for a snapshot copy), registers the folder the owner picks under an opaque location ID, and answers that ID, or that the owner cancelled. The folder never crosses the API as a path, title or storage key (API-S-005); the UI names the ID in the create, open and snapshot-copy routes. One dialog is open at a time: a request while one is open is refused 409 conflict (`dialog_open`), as is a picked folder the host cannot register (`location_refused`). A host without a dialog (filesquid-server) answers 503 unavailable. Each request is journaled once as `library.location.choose`: succeeded with the location ID, cancelled, or failed with its error code.

200.description: The folder the owner picked, by its opaque location ID, or that they cancelled.

409.description: A folder dialog is already open, or the picked folder cannot hold a library (`conflict`).

post.summary: Copy a file into a new file
post.description: Copy the file `file_id` at its head into a new file (API-S-011, SRS-F-062): a new FileId and stored name `original/<new-uuid>.<ext>` in the new file's own object `files/<new-id>`, published as its version v1. The copy keeps the display name, the original name, the media type and every statement; its one import entry is the source's latest entry rebound to the copy, and its record names the source as the asserted statement `dcterms:source` = `urn:uuid:<source-id>@vN`. The source never changes, and the copy is a new file with its own home collection (its display name is the source's). A source over 67,108,864 bytes is refused (400) until a streamed copy exists. The copy is journaled as `file.copy` with opaque IDs only; a refusal is journaled once. Command (Task API-F2.13, API-S-002): the body carries a `CommandEnvelope` beside the input (schema version 1; an opaque operation_id of 1 to 128 letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` or `:`; scope `library:<library_id>`). The expected revision is the head version of the source file's object `urn:uuid:<file_id>` that the caller read; the copy's own object is new. A stale revision is answered 409 with a `conflict` outcome and changes nothing. A 200 answer is a `CommandOutcome` of the same operation_id (`committed`) whose `result` is what the command made. A repeated operation_id of the same command that changed something answers its first answer again, before the revision is checked, with no second change; the same operation_id with another route, library or input is refused (400). A refusal stores no receipt, so its retry is evaluated again. Receipts are kept in memory while the host runs, at most 10,000. Destination and home (Task API-F2.14, API-S-011, API-S-026): the input names `collection_id` (required) and optionally `folder`; without a collection the request is refused 400 invalid_request (`destination_required`) and an unknown or foreign collection 404 not_found (`collection_not_found`), each before any byte is staged and journaled once. After the file's object is committed, the file is registered in the collection snapshot with its home collection, its logical path `<folder>/<name>` and its object, under the request's operation ID, as one snapshot version journaled `library.files.register`; the answer's `collection_id` and `path` name where it went. A path already taken in the collection, a recoverably deleted file's included, is never refused or overwritten: the new file takes the first free number beside it (`photo-1.jpg`, `archive-1.tar.gz`, `report-1`, `.env-1`, `.config-1.json`); after 9,999 numbers the request is refused 409 conflict (`path_suffix_exhausted`) and a numbered name over 255 bytes 400 invalid_request (`name_too_long`), with no change. A crash between the file's object and its registration leaves the operation's reserved file ID; a retry under the same operation ID completes that file once. Each success publishes `navigation.change` for the folder that holds the file. A host without home collections answers 503.

200.description: The copy and its first version.

get.summary: One page of a view of a node
get.description: The view operation (API-S-011, SRS-F-062): one page of the files of a library, collection or virtual-collection node, in a stable order. A library node's `all` view shows its collections and virtual collections as folder rows beside its unfiled files; a collection node shows its files, a virtual-collection node its members, and the `deleted` view the node's recoverably deleted files with no folder rows. The views home, personal, recent, favorites, shares and tags are not available yet (400). Each page sorts the whole scope again (at most 10,000 files, MAX_VIEW_FILES, and 1,000 folder rows; `complete` is false beyond that or when a file could not be read) and starts after the cursor's row, so rows never repeat. A missing value (a folder's size, a file the caller never opened) sorts after every value in both directions; ties break by name, then identifier. `modified_by_me` and `opened_by_me` come only from the caller's own succeeded journal entries (changes; content-handle mints and single-file downloads). A cursor made for other parameters is refused (400); a cursor of a view whose rows or their order changed since it was made is refused as conflict (409), so a row never repeats or is skipped, and the client starts again without a cursor. An unknown, malformed or unreadable node is 404; a node of another kind is 400. A successful read is not journaled; a refusal is journaled once.

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: A library, collection or virtual-collection node handle, as the navigation listing gave it.

parameters.name: view
parameters.description: The view; all when absent.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The sort key; name when absent.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: The direction; ascending when absent.

parameters.name: folders
parameters.description: Where folder rows go; on_top when absent.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Only rows whose name contains this text, compared without case; at most 256 bytes.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The next_cursor of the previous page of the same view.

get.summary: The bytes a collection's history keeps
get.description: Storage use per collection (API-S-011, SRS-F-062): each distinct content of each file whose home is the collection counted once, hidden and deleted files included, within 10,000 files and 100,000 contents (`truncated` says when a bound stopped the count or a file could not be read). An unknown or unreadable collection is 404. A successful read is not journaled; a refusal is journaled once.

parameters.name: collection_id
parameters.description: The collection.

get.summary: Search the files the caller may read
get.description: The search operation: the files and folder rows of the caller's readable scope that match q, as rows like GET /api/v1/files/view (display names, API-S-027; collections and virtual collections as folder rows). Grammar (API-S-012, SRS-F-063): terms separated by white space; a term is a word, a quoted phrase ("Client deck") or an operator name:value whose value may be quoted; a leading - excludes what the term matches; operator names compare without case, and text containing a colon is quoted. Free text matches the display name and every dcterms: value. Operators: type: (image, video, audio, text, document: PDF, RTF and the Microsoft Office, OOXML and OpenDocument formats; folder), in: (a collection's title), title: (dcterms:title), owner:me, creator: (dcterms:creator, whole value), tag: (dcterms:subject), is:deleted, is:unfiled, before: and after: (the head version's date in the caller's zone), createdbefore: and createdafter: (YYYY-MM-DD; the capture date from exif:DateTimeOriginal, else dcterms:created: a value with a zone is an instant compared by its date in the caller's zone, a value without one by the calendar date it states, so no instant is invented), source: (dcterms:source), size> and size< (an integer and an optional B, KB, MB or GB in powers of 1024). Every value and name compared is normalised to Unicode NFC and then to lower case (each character's lower-case mapping, then NFC again), so a decomposed (NFD) name matches a composed query; diacritics are not folded. An unknown operator (generator: among them, since this build has no c2pa module) is refused as invalid_request naming it, never matched as an empty filter. Operators of the grammar this host cannot answer, is:favorite, owner: naming another user and the filesquid-server operators sharedwith:, to:, from: and pendingowner:, are refused as unavailable (503) naming the operator, the disabled-module error of API-S-007. The scope (the repository by default, or a library, collection or virtual-collection node) is permission-filtered before anything is read or ranked (SRS-NFR-004): an unreadable library, collection or file is never read or examined, and a caller who may not read the repository cannot search it (404). Relevance (the default order, most relevant first) adds for each free-text term 3 when the display name holds it, 2 when a dcterms:title does and 1 when a dcterms: value other than the title does (the three add up); any view sort key may replace it without changing the matches. Paging and cursors follow GET /api/v1/files/view: the order is stable, a cursor of other parameters is refused (400) and a cursor of results that changed is refused as conflict (409). Bounds: q is at most 1,024 bytes (MAX_QUERY_BYTES) and 32 terms (MAX_QUERY_TERMS); one search examines at most 1,000 libraries (MAX_SEARCH_LIBRARIES) and 10,000 files (MAX_SEARCH_FILES), reading one more catalog entry, never examined, only to learn that the scope is larger, and complete is false when a bound left files out or a file could not be read; the caller's own times read at most 20 journal pages per library (MAX_JOURNAL_PAGES). There is no separate index: each search reads the catalog and the files' OCFL records, so its answer always follows canonical state. Content (full-text) search is not offered yet. A successful search is not journaled; a refusal is journaled once.

parameters.description: The query: free text and operators of the grammar above; at most 1,024 bytes and 32 terms.

parameters.name: node
parameters.description: The repository, library, collection or virtual-collection node handle searched; the repository when absent.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The order; relevance when absent.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: The direction; descending for relevance and ascending for the other orders when absent.

parameters.name: folders
parameters.description: Where folder rows go; on_top when absent.

parameters.name: zone
parameters.description: The caller's zone for date boundaries: Z or a fixed offset from -14:00 to +14:00, such as -08:00; UTC when absent.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The next_cursor of the previous page of the same search.

get.summary: Durable jobs
get.description: At most 100 durable jobs (limit, default and most 100; a larger limit answers 100), newest first, optionally of one kind and in one state, marked truncated when more match (API-S-037). There is no cursor: narrow the listing by kind and state to reach older jobs. A kind outside 1 to 128 characters, a limit outside 1 to 1000 or an unknown state is refused as invalid_request. A job is created by the route of its kind (for example POST /api/v1/imports). The views never carry a job's source identity, checkpoint, lease holder or fencing number. A filter that cannot be read is refused as invalid_request and journaled as job.refused.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Only jobs of this kind.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only jobs in this state.

get.summary: One durable job
get.description: One job's view: its state, whether it is paused, the control asked of it, its progress, attempts and error code (API-S-037).

post.summary: Pause a job
post.description: Pause the job: a pending job is held and does not start until it is resumed; a running job's worker suspends at its next checkpoint, keeping it, and the job then stays paused. Pausing a paused job changes nothing. Journaled as job.paused; a refusal as job.refused (API-S-037).

post.summary: Resume a job
post.description: Clear the pause of the job and hand a pending job to the worker the host installed for its kind, which resumes it from its checkpoint without repeating completed work (scheduled true); with no such worker the job stays pending for the next launch (scheduled false). Journaled as job.resumed; a refusal as job.refused (API-S-037).

post.summary: Cancel a job
post.description: Cancel the job: a pending job, or a running one whose lease has ended, is cancelled at once (job.cancelled); a running job's worker stops at its next checkpoint, after which the job is cancelled (job.cancel_requested). A run that suspends or whose lease expires under a cancel request is cancelled. A refusal is journaled as job.refused (API-S-037).

post.summary: Rename a library
post.description: Renames a library this host opened (API-S-038) and answers its facts. The name follows the rules of API-S-019: 1 to 1,024 bytes, not blank, no control characters (invalid_request with the code invalid_name). A library this host never opened is 404 not_found (library_not_found). A rename is journaled as library.rename with the library ID only, never the name; a rename to the current name changes nothing and is not journaled. A host without a library registry, filesquid-server among them, answers 503 unavailable. Takes a CommandEnvelope beside its input (Task API-F2.19, API-S-002): scope library:<library_id>, expected_revision the current revision of the library, which must be open on this host (a remembered library that is not open now is 404 not_found, library_not_open); a stale revision is a conflict outcome with no change. Answers a committed CommandOutcome for the envelope's operation_id with the facts as result, at the advanced revision when the name changed; a changed name stores a receipt, so a repeated operation_id answers it again with no second change, and a rename to the current name stores none.

200.description: The library's facts after the rename, as a committed outcome.

get.summary: A library's name and free space
get.description: Answers {library_id, name, free_bytes, free_bytes_reason} of a library this host opened (API-S-038): free_bytes is the free space of the volume that holds its storage root, or null with free_bytes_reason volume_unreadable (the volume could not be read; every build other than Linux and macOS until DE-F3.3) or not_local. Readable by anyone who may read the library, not by administrators only. An unknown library, or one the caller may not read, is 404 not_found; each refusal is journaled once as library.facts. A host without a library registry, filesquid-server among them, answers 503 unavailable. Never a path, storage key or location ID.

parameters.name: library
parameters.description: The library ID.

get.summary: The libraries this host opened
get.description: First keeps only the libraries this host opened that the caller may read, then lists at most 20 of them, newest first (API-S-038): each with its ID, name, last opened time (RFC 3339 UTC), whether it is open now and the free bytes of its volume when its folder is reachable. Never a path, storage key or location ID. A host without a library registry, filesquid-server among them, answers 503 unavailable, journaled once as library.recent.

get.summary: The planned files of an import plan
get.description: API-S-036 Review. The files of the open plan, at most 1,000 per page with a cursor, in the plan's order, each with its display name (its base name, never a folder path), its size, whether the library already holds it (the job skips it) and whether its name will be numbered because its path is taken (API-S-011). An unknown, expired, discarded or started plan is 404 not_found (`plan_not_found`); a limit outside 1 to 1000 or an unknown query field is 400 invalid_request; a host without an import dialog answers 503. A refusal is journaled once as `import.plan_items`; the display names never appear in an error or a journal entry.

200.description: One page of the planned files.

post.summary: Start the import job of a reviewed plan
post.description: API-S-036 Review. Takes no body and no CommandEnvelope (API-S-002, owner decision 2026-10-30): the plan ID is the idempotency key, and the answer's outcome names the plan request's operation ID. Asks the host to submit one durable import job (API-S-033, kind `import`) for the open plan and start it in the background; answers `pending` with `import: started` and the job. A repeated start of the same plan answers the same job again and starts nothing. An unknown, expired or discarded plan is 404 not_found (`plan_not_found`); a source that changed since the plan was made is 409 conflict (`source_changed`) and the plan stays open for review; a host that cannot run the job now, or without an import dialog, answers 503. Each start is journaled once as `import.start`: `succeeded` with the job ID, or `failed` with its code. Takes no body: the plan carries the operation ID of the request that made it.

409.description: The picked source changed since the plan was made (conflict, journal code `source_changed`); the plan stays open.

delete.description: API-S-036 Review. Takes no body and no CommandEnvelope (API-S-002, owner decision 2026-10-30): the plan ID is the idempotency key; a repeated discard is 404 not_found (`plan_not_found`) and changes nothing. Discards the open plan, changing nothing else: no byte was staged and no job is made; the plan's operation ID then answers 404 not_found (`plan_not_found`). The host discards an open plan on its own 1 hour after it was made. An unknown, expired, discarded or started plan is 404 not_found (`plan_not_found`); a host without an import dialog answers 503. Each discard is journaled once as `import.discard`.

get.summary: The files of an upload job
get.description: API-S-037 Per-file progress (owner answer 6 of 2026-10-22, "Yes, report progress per file"). The files of the job, at most 1,000 per page with a cursor, in the job's order, each with its display name (no path), its destination folder, its state (`queued`, `copying` with bytes done of total, `copied`, `skipped` as already in the library, or `failed` with its error code), its bytes and its size. A job without files answers an empty page. An unknown job is 404 not_found (journaled as job.refused); a limit outside 1 to 1000 or an unknown query field is 400 invalid_request; a host that keeps no per-file progress answers 503.

200.description: One page of the job's files.

post.summary: Retry one failed file of an upload job
post.description: API-S-037 Per-file progress. Puts the failed file back to `queued` and hands a pending job to the runner the host installed for its kind (`scheduled` says whether it did; a running job's worker picks the file up itself). Not a command envelope (owner decision 2 of 2026-10-23): it names the state it asks for, takes no body and answers the job view, so repeating it changes nothing and hands nothing to the runner; a file that is not failed is left as it is. A paused job is refused 409 conflict (`job_paused`) and nothing changes: resume it first. A finished or cancel-requested job refuses the retry as the controls do; an unknown job or item is 404 not_found. Each file put back is journaled once as `job.item_retried` under the job's operation ID, with the job and the item as targets; a retry that changes nothing is not journaled; a refusal is journaled as job.refused. The display name never appears in an error or a journal entry.

200.description: The job after the retry, and whether it was handed to its runner.

post.summary: Retry every failed file of an upload job
post.description: API-S-037 Per-file progress. Puts every failed file of the job back to `queued` and hands a pending job to its runner (`scheduled`); a retry that puts no file back changes nothing and hands nothing to the runner. Not a command envelope (owner decision 2 of 2026-10-23): no body, the job view answered, idempotent. A paused job is refused 409 conflict (`job_paused`) and nothing changes; a finished or cancel-requested job refuses the retry as the controls do; an unknown job is 404 not_found. Each file put back is journaled once as `job.item_retried` under the job's operation ID.

200.description: The job after the retry, and whether it was handed to its runner.

missed.description: How many events this subscriber did not receive.

The router-wide fallbacks use 404 not_found (path not in the contract) and 405 method_not_allowed (method not documented for the path). Version.description: The version: head (the default) or one such as v1.

Range.name: Range
Range.description: One byte range: bytes=a-b, bytes=a- or bytes=-n. A malformed header, another unit or several ranges are ignored.

NavigationNode.name: node
NavigationNode.description: The opaque handle of the node whose children to list, as an earlier answer gave it (clients never parse it). Absent: the host's repository level. An unknown, malformed or unreadable handle answers one identical 404 not_found.

JobId.name: job
JobId.description: A job ID as a job route or a job-starting route answered it.

PlanId.name: plan_id
PlanId.description: An import plan ID as `POST /api/v1/imports` answered it.

JobItemId.name: item
JobItemId.description: An item ID of a job, as the job items route lists it (the file ID the host minted when it planned the import).

Unauthorized.description: No credentials were presented (unauthorized, reason missing_credentials).

Forbidden.description: The credentials are not accepted (reason invalid_credentials) or do not permit this operation (reason not_permitted).

HostNotDescribed.description: The host has not described itself yet (unavailable; retryable).

NotFound.description: Nothing is recorded there, or the library, object, version, folder or file does not exist (not_found). One answer for all of them.

HistoryUnavailable.description: The host has not installed its history source yet, or its storage cannot be read now (unavailable; retryable).

Conflict.description: The write would change nothing, another change is staged, the object changed at the same paths meanwhile, a file has that path, or the head is incomplete (conflict); nothing was published.

RangeNotSatisfiable.description: The range starts at or past the end of the file (range_not_satisfiable). Carries Content-Range: bytes */<length>.

FilesUnavailable.description: The library's storage is not reachable, or the host has not installed its file service yet (unavailable; retryable).

ContentDenied.description: The one identical denial of the content route (forbidden, reason invalid_credentials, not retryable) for any unusable handle: unknown, malformed, missing, expired, evicted, revoked, or one whose minting credential no longer may read files. Same status, headers and body every time; a HEAD denial has no body. No file is read first.

LibraryNotFound.description: The location ID is not one the host registered (location_not_found), or the library is not open on this host (library_not_open) (not_found). The answer's code is not_found; the journal entry names which.

LibraryConflict.description: Refused by a rule about the storage root, the destination or the consent (conflict); nothing was written. The journal entry names the rule: root_not_empty, not_a_storage_root, git_in_root, destination_not_empty, snapshot_unreadable, destination_overlaps_library, location_in_use, library_already_open, library_mismatch, too_many_libraries, consent_required or consent_mismatch.

LibraryUnavailable.description: The library's storage, the repair ledger or the reservation store is not reachable now, a head is still being published (snapshot_incomplete), or the host has not installed its library commands yet (unavailable; retryable).

PayloadTooLarge.description: The request body is larger than the route accepts (payload_too_large).

RateLimited.description: Over the route's rate bound (rate_limited). Retry after Retry-After seconds.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds until a request is admitted again.

PreferencesUnavailable.description: The host keeps no preferences yet, or their store cannot be reached (unavailable; retryable).

JobConflict.description: The job cannot take this control now (conflict): it has finished (job_finished), it is being cancelled (cancel_requested), or it is running and was not paused (job_running); the journaled refusal names the rule. Nothing changed.

JobsUnavailable.description: The host runs no durable jobs yet, or its job store is not reachable (unavailable, retryable).

CommandConflict.description: A `conflict` outcome of the command's operation_id: the expected revision is stale, the command would change nothing, another change reached the object first, or a command with that operation_id is still running; nothing was published.

PlanNotFound.description: No open import plan has this ID: it is unknown, expired, discarded or already started (not_found, journal code `plan_not_found`).

JobOrItemNotFound.description: No job has this ID, or the job has no file with this item ID (not_found).

JobRetryConflict.description: The job cannot take a retry now (conflict): it has finished (job_finished), it is being cancelled (cancel_requested), or it is paused and must be resumed first (job_paused); the journaled refusal names the rule. Nothing changed.

LibraryCommandConflict.description: A `conflict` outcome of the command's operation_id: the expected revision is stale, a rule about the storage root or the destination refused the command (the journal entry names it), or a command with that operation_id is still running; nothing was written.

bearerAuth.description: Deny-by-default credential required by every operation. filesquid-desktop: the per-launch token the host generates at every launch and gives only to its own webviews (window.__FILESQUID_LAUNCH_TOKEN__). filesquid-server: the administrator token (FILESQUID_ADMIN_TOKEN or <data dir>/admin-token) until accounts, sessions and groups arrive. A WebSocket upgrade may carry it as the subprotocol filesquid.bearer.<token>.
